newsitem.title: USA: Beverly to appeal court decision on strike.
newsitem.headline: Beverly to appeal court decision on strike.

text.p: Beverly Enterprises Inc said it will file an appeal with the Third Circuit Court in Philadelphia to overturn a federal judge's decision that an April 1996 strike against the company was legal.

Beverly said it is requesting expedited consideration and will also file for a stay pending resolution of the appeal of the court order, which required the company to reinstate workers who were on strike.
Of the 389 workers who were replaced during the strike, Beverly has already rehired 339, Beverly group vice president Wayne Chapman said.
"What the judge's order does is advance that process," he said and could result in some additional internal reassignments.

"We believe that the Federal District Court was mistaken in failing to recognize that the behavior by the unions and the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) is improper and that the strike against our Pennsylvania facilities was illegal," Chapman said.
He said the unions struck Beverly's Pennsylvania facilities on April 1, 1996, after refusing since November, 1995 to negotiate new contracts with individual Beverly facilities as required by law.
The union has continued to frustrate negotiations in recent months.
"Despite the unions' marked unwillingness to negotiate, Beverly has, in good faith, rehired many of the replaced workers," he said.
Chapman said if Beverly wins its appeal, it may seek to recover damages from the union.
